service_text: Found circuit a and b overcharged circuit a has 34 degree sub cooling and circuit b has 29 degree sub cooling RTU has several high pressure alerts and high pressure alarms removed refrigerant from both circuits now circuit a has 15 degree sub cooling and circuit b has 13 degree sub cooling

8/12/13 RTU #6 Unit is tripping B circuit on high head, A is also high but not tripping, Will return with equipment.  8/13/19 RTU #6 Recovered 1.5 pounds of refrigerant from circuit B and .5 from circuit A. Sensors for OAT and RAT were reading swapped. Swapped sensors at main board to read correctly.

Arrived to identify problem with unit. He???s pressure alerts were found. After performing multiple checks and discussing with CARRIER ROLE, I was advised to entice 1# of refrigerant from each circuit. Advised customer of work performed and to keep us posted in the event of a continued issue with the unit.

Check unit # 2 serial # 0317U49159 and let it run in test mode on A side compressors for 15 to 20 minutes and started to see a very sharp rise in head pressure. Looked at charging chart in service manual and found circuit A was over charged from factory, and adjust charge on Circuit A. Also check unit # 1 serial # 0417U49163 and unit # 3 serial # 0317U49157 and found both of theses units were over charged on circuits A , adjust charge on both units. Unit # 1 also had a sensor fault alarm and I traced back to a bad factory connection at board and repaired connection .   Also set baud rate on chiller from 38400 to 9600 so building controls could read chiller bac net points.

AC-G1 TRIPPING ON HIGH HEAD- UNIT CAME OVERCHARGED FROM FACTORY 48A3/ 0417U44749. Arrived on site, check in with customer, found circuit B tripping out on high discharge pressure, checked sub cooling and found it to 22, recovery 1 lb. of 410 refrigerant and set up sub cooling to 14. Verified AC unit for operation and all working fine at this time, cleaned work area and informed customer of complete work.

Continue to work on unit. Returning to job site tomorrow.  Issue with RT-2.Static pressure not maintaining supply fan not ramping up.Circuits A and B tripped out on high pressure switch.Remove 1 lb of refrigerant from each circuit.All condenser fans running.Check amps were ok.Test fan.Mark from Testcomm was saying unit not maintaining static pressure setpoint.Look into issue.  Looked at configurations.Looked at input table found that the static pressure reset was in the force mode.Release force.Fan started to ramp up with a set point of 1.2 .Had Jeremy change static pressure setpoint from computer.Verify that fan was ramping correctly.Jeremy put set point at 1.2 static pressure.  Met up with Jeremy from Standard.Go over issue static pressure issue.Had him change the static pressure setpoint to 1.2 fan ramping down.Not working correctly.
unit is overcharged from the factor labor for the   techs time onsite, also the recover of the unit   and the evac/recharge of the unit..
CIRCUIT A OVERCHARGED CAUSING LOCKOUTS AT COLLEGE.   RECOVERED 2 LBS OUT OF CIRCUIT TO CORRECT.
UNIT OVERCHARGED FROM THE FACTORY. HAD TO REMOVED 2.5   EACH CIRCUIT TO KEEP ONLINE.

Checked pressure in a couple different locations to make sure not an exv . In test mode  The Relative humidity valve RHV. Would open at same time as compressor few minutes later then would shut. Yet I am not energizing & de-energizing, do not believe that this should happen while in test mode Did not get a answer from Roll on this! Removed  a little over 4 lbs from B circuit.

Rooftop unit having alarms, run tested unit to check operation. The unit???s controller kept shutting off the unit, removed controller and run unit with a jumper. The unit did not fail nor generated any alarms.  High head pressure alarms, when unit call for 100% cool the head pressure goes upwards of 600psi tripping the safety switch.  Removed 3 Lbs or refrigerant 410a as per service engineers. Apparently the factory is overcharging the rooftop unit. Overcharged is generating high pressure alarms.
Unit overcharged from factory.   Contractor pulled all refrigerant,   evacuated and recharged.
Monday May 7th. Drove on site and gained access to building roof. Brought tools up to the roof and proceeded to remove 1.5 lbs of r410a from circuit A.

6-22-18   Reclaimed 35 lbs Of R410 and non condensates. from CKT B also had reclaimed trip on high head with 10 lbs reclaimed.   Weighed in 25 lbs virgin R410.   Checked operation all ok  Exchange reclaimer tanks
RTU found to be overcharged in both circuits. Removed refrigerant from both circuits.

RTU 2.  Startup.  Arrived.  Circuit B failure alarms.  Service test B1.  Pressures steady for a moment and quickly jumps to 600# and trips on high head.  Service test B2.  Same alarm.  Service test both.  Same alarm.  Strapped gauges on circuit to verify operation of discharge pressure transducer.  Gauges reading same as Navigator.  We've come across this issue many times at startup.  Carrier Role advises us to pull charge, replace C165S liquid line drier, pull deep vacuum and charge with new 410a.  Disabled B1, B2 in configurations.  Completed startup.  RTU in vent mode upon departure.  Will return to make repair and move forward with circuit B.

On arrival found several alarms, T-126 A circuit high pressure trip. P-051 A circuit #1 comp failure. p-056 B circuit #2 failure. Performed test on both circuits using service test. All compressor running in the correct rotation. Startup A circuit with 1 compressor running pressure 148/273 with 2 compressor running head pressure spikes and trips high pressure control. Started B circuit 1 compressor 159/265,2 compressor 129/330. This circuit appears to be running good. Checked filters for construction dust ok. Found wire to humidity control off and armed to sheetmetal panel. Taped up for now. A- circuit might be over charged. Will recommend pulling charge and weight it. For now will disable A2 compressor to keep that circuit online. Checked temp drop across drier it seems ok. Roll case # 00849917. Talked to Jim from roll, he recommended double checking charge using book 12T. Remove frown in 1/2 lbs increments. Possible non condemnable in system. Anything further contact Tom Hoskins.
Balanced refrigerant charge in circuits A and B removed 5 pounds from each circuit as per unit charging instructions

Found both compressors on circuit B going into alarm due to high head pressure which is most likely due to being overcharged. RTU was also going into alarm for loss of communication to the belimo actuator. Tried to recalibrate the actuator but it went into alarm again. Verified that there was power being supplied to the actuator. Will return tomorrow to recover some refrigerant from circuit B and to continue troubleshooting actuator.  Found circuit A and B tripping on compressor failure. Found circuit B was tripping almost immediately on high pressure. I checked operation of the condenser modulating vale. Found no problems. Removed refrigerant and the circuit stayed on line but was not cooling properly. Will return to check.  Recovered a total of 15 pounds from circuit B and verified charge for both circuits using charging chart. Also found unit kept going into re-heat mode so looked in the book to verify operation of re-heat. Also found actuator with loss of communication because it had been disconnected and wired to JCI controls.  Found the unit running in reheat mode to control humidity causing higher supply air temperatures. I checked the refrigerant charge for both circuits and adjusted to the charging chart. I found the economizer actuator had been disconnected and taken over by JCI. I disabled the economizer to stop the alarms.  Came out and found cktb off on high head pressure. ckta was running, temps and pressures ok. Reset cktb pressure and temps ok.all cond fans staging correctly. Found economizer actuator disconnected from comfort link control, and being controlled from EMS which is Johnson controls. Also called role and opened case#01648351 .rtu is operating at this time. Will comeback to further troubleshoot.

Arrived on site checked in with contact Juan with installing contractor company. Checked comfort link for alarms for multiple alarms on P126, P127 which are high head pressure trips. Contractor will pull out refrigerant from both circuits and adjust per charging scale. Verified thermostat stages on all 4 compressors A1, B1. Cleaned up job site and checked out.  Arrived on site checked in with contacts and waited for building to be did armed. Gained access to RTU 1, M# 48A4D040-FM621EQ   S# 3417U45907 met with installing contractor.   Checked alarms none present at this time. Prior alarm history had head pressure trips, adjusted refrigerant charge and recovered 2# R410a per circuit. Monitored operation with all compressors in operation.  Arrived on site checked in with contact Bob gained access to RTU 1, upon arrival found unit operating in cooling. Per customer said over weekend it blew a 5 amp. On block FU-6/FU-7 Control fuse, checked fuse block and tight, fuses are FNQ-R-5 600 V, Checked amp draws off line side at .8/.9 amps and load side with unit off at 2.4 amps, once compressors staged on amps drop, A1 @ 1.8, B1@ 1.2, A2@ .6, B2@.3 amps. Ran unit in test mode operations and ran unit independently unable to duplicate issue at this time. Checked alarms history found T424 multiple times found thermostat not sending fan signal on a call for cooling and causing alarms each time, resets and normal operation continues.   Alarm A404 for fire shutdown and verified with customer said they caused those alarms. Alarms for high pressure have not returned since refrigerant charge adjusted. Advised customer of findings and will have installing contractor replace thermostat and verify wiring. Cleaned up job site and checked out.
LABOR FOR CCS TO RECOVER REFRIGERANT OUT OF THIS UNIT BECAUSE IT WAS OVER CHARGED FROM THE FACTORY.

Unit tripping HPS on both circuits. Removed charge from circuit B & found it charged   to name plate. Had high sub-cooling & low superheat. Re-charged circuit to 10* sub-  cooling and 8* uperheat with 9# 10oz R410A.  Had to do the same thing with Circuit A    Gregg Arlt approved to pay labor costs  CG# 1005922
Adjusted charge for altitude as per technical service on two circuits. Started and checked operation.  Spoke to Joe Caslake regarding micro channel coils. Adjusted refrigerant charges on units.
Pre-Auth - Empower $ to true up Robertson   Morrison "warranty costs for chasing HP issues   on the roof @ Google in A2
Add iVu per Bob Henderson to assist in Remote diagnostics / Troubleshooting of RTU's @ Google
Monday checked out unit #2 drive is not working found fuses blown. Replaced fuses. Found motor over amping due to short duct run and no sp transducer connected, adjusted max hertz and amperage.
TOP PANEL WAS UNREPAIRABLE  REPLACECED UNDER WARRANTY

Arrived. Checked in with customer. Located CU. Customer complaint of leak in circuit A condenser coil. Unbuttoned panels. Customer leak checked recently with nitrogen. Circuit A 270#. Added more nitrogen to achieve 340#. Customer and I could not locate leak with nitrogen, leak detector and bubbles. We decided to isolate condenser at factory installed suction, liquid ball valves. We also isolated liquid line at outlet side of drier core canister at field installed ball valve. The circuit is isolated in three areas. Condenser, liquid line and suction/evaporator. Circuit A contactors CB off and coil wires pulled from contactors. Customer will monitor and report back to CCS.

10/18/18   Went to Lennox parts plus and confirmed with Corey at Lennox and Kendal at Carrier the accurate parts order list for parts needed for repairs on job.10/23/18   Arrived at location.i assisted Allen Henderson in testing duct static pressure,blower amp draw and blower speed RPM
DOA ISSUES: T431 ??? Motor Starter Protector Trip, A432 ??? Motor Starter Protector Lockout (no building pressure control), T110 ??? Circuit A loss of charge, T411 ??? Exhaust Fan VFD Fault

Unit going into low saturated suction temperature alarms. Found the cause was the blower motor drive in alarm for under voltage. Rest alarm checked all parameters, megged out motor, tightened all electrical connections. No problem found, tested drive voltage and amps good, enabled fan status monitoring to shut down unit upon fan failure.
tightened up all connections. reset checked operation. could not duplicate overcurrent or undervolt alarm. changed config unit sfs to yes and on sratic pressure rise.

Checked out unit #1. Found drive tripped out in over current. Ohm out motor, good. Tighten all connections from the drive back to the breaker. Checked drive configurations, all ok. Reset drive and started unit. Turned on fan status monitoring. Recommend checking power on this side of building all units drives have tripped on under voltage and over amperage.
JOB SITE VISIT TO TROUBLESHOOT ALARMS

Drove to customer site and gained access to rooftop equipment. Found circuit A off at breaker . Restored power and cycled circuit A compressors. No issues found . Sound is from digital scroll operation . Informed customer of findings.

Unit tripped yesterday. Customer cycled power to it. Came right back on. Checked electrical connections, looked for anything out of place. Checked pressures, temperatures and amp draws. Circuit a: 9degrees superheat 15degrees subcooling. 12 amps on compressor. Circuit b: 15 degrees superheat 18 degrees subcooling we amps on compressor. Condenser fan motors were drawing 1 amp. Found nothing out of ordinary on unit.

rove to site. Checked in with customer. Customer explained that he heard a banging noise in the ceiling at start up in the morning. It then went away a short time later. Brought tools to roof. Checked unit operation. Unit running. Supply fan VFD running at 100%. Static pressure reading was 0.3". Set point was set to 0.5. Called controls contractor to set static to 1". Pressure would not raise. VFD still at 100%. Controls contractor said he was only getting 25% flow to his VAV boxes. I turned unit off and checked inside unit of loose fan belt, pullies, or anything that looked off. Everything looked ok. Ran unit again. Verified VFD running at 100%. Amps were 27 when full load is 40. Seems like the air is not getting to VAVs or pressure pick up tube. Almost as duct work has fallen off of curb. Need to verify connection. Also, recommend getting an air balancer out to balance system. Explained findings to customer and controls contractor. Brought tools down from roof and locked up ladder. Checked out with customer.

Arrived site and checked in with customer. Customer mentioned that compressor A1 making noise and vibrating. A/C #1 east side. Went through electrical connections and tightened contacts used megger to check compressor windings all normal. Checked for correct voltage and everything looks normal. Ran system in test mode one compressor at a time and all 4 at once all normal pressures and temperatures did not see anything making noise or vibrating notified customer if it happens again to shut compressor down and call us out. No problems at this time
Troubleshoot the power exhaust VFD tripping off on fault 2202 ???start enable missing???

Troubleshoot VFD faults. Found no alarms pertaining to the VFDs at the Marque level. Found multiple ground fault alarms at both VFDs.     Contacted tech support who directed me to check the drives for the latest software version. Both were current.     I checked the machine for proper grounding/bonding. All checked ok. I checked for any signs of corrosion or moisture in the motors. None found.

Relief fan not running. Noted 2 of 3 line fuses blown. Replaced fuses. Drive shows - - - on display. Attempted to access programming of VFD, password listed in literature would not work. Looked up manufacturer manual, attempted password listed. No success. Contacted support, (case # 01390826) they could not offer solution further than steps already taken. Contacted drive manufacturer, was told 475 was emergency password. Worked with support and found parameter 10, and PID Control select wrong. Corrected both. Unit runs and follows input signal. VFD will not stop fan with minimum signal. Will have to add analog relay to stop drive at 0% signal.
Installed my laptop on unit to check through field assisted. Found no alarms present at this time. Ran unit through test function to make sure no problems.

Once on site I checked in with the custmer and we got roof access. I then went to AC-5 and found T617 and a T927 alarm coming and going. I then checked the E.GAP setting and found it was set to 0% but the default should be 5% and the E.TMR was set to 0 seconds but the default should be 20sec. I change it to default setting and calibrated the dampers. The alarm when away. I then ran circuit A with both compressor and found the head pressure would clime really high in the upper 400 psig then come back down randomly even with all condenser fans running constantly with no pressure drop across the drier. I suspect the unit is ether overcharged or the refrigerant may be contaminated. I open a warranty ticket and recovered all the refrigerant. I found the refrigerant did not match the pressure temperature chart with R410a so I will replace it with new refrigerant. I started a vacuum on the circuit A and will run it over the weekend. I then cleaned up and checked out with the customer.  Once on site I checked the vacuum level and found it at 440 microns. I then turned on the heater for the unit so I could get a better load. I then checked the fan cycling setting to make sure they where set to the default value. I then charged in new refrigerant to factory charge of 47.6 lb of R-410a. I then ran circuit A at full capacity and competed the start up paperwork and for 20 min it was running fine. Then after running circuit B and completing the start up paperwork for that circuit and seeing it run fine I went back to A and found the head pressure to swing 75 psig when the first condenser fans stage was running and swing 50 psig when all condenser fans where running. I watched over the unit and found the head pressure for A never got high enough to trip the high pressure switch but it was only 60F outside. I will have to come back to figure out what could be causing the swing in pressure. I then cleaned up and checked out with the customer.  Once on site I met up with the contractor to get unit access. I then found the unit shutd

Removed filters and relief damper assembly. Determined removal of part of filter gram at upper and lower sections would leave space for installation of upper frame filters. Upper filters secure in framework after modification. Sent photos to Larry P after completion.

I found the unit tripped on high head pressure. I checked and found the motormaster 5 is bad and needs replaced. I checked both fan motors, ok. I wired around the motormaster and got the unit running.  Replaced bad VFD for condensor fan motors. Restart unit and check rotation -ok . Unit is cooling.

Checked and found alarm codes P126. Found motor master fan drive blowing fuses. Isolated drive and bypassed as needed. Ordered a new drive will return next to make repairs.    Shut down unit. Locked out. Installed new motor master. Started up unit checked operation ok.

Return to address issues with 48A series units. We began with unit #4. Performing a start up per manufacturer requirements. Upon beginning start up we were unable to move air through the unit. Went down to check and found most of the supply duct still covered with plastic covers. We had to go around and remove them so we could get proper air supply. Contractor said unit was ready. Unit #3 was the unit that had the pulley come off. Took part numbers and will order new parts. Also checked unit operation, there was no issues with the operation of the unit. Checked unit #4 and this unit also had no issues with it???s operation. Unit #5 this had a loud noise coming from it when running. We checked the unit and there was no noise. Ramped the fan to 100 percent and still no noise other than normal. Ran through the operation, no problems. After speaking to balancer and control techs from TEC, they found that plastic was still on the return grille. Mechanical tech removed before we came out. This unit also still doesn???t have a space sensor installed in the space as well. There is also the linkage that still has to be set up for the RTUs. According to the TEC tech Dan everything has be heating just fine after the pulley problem was taken care of. Will order pulley for unit 3.
WHY - area not cooling   FOUND - short to ground  DONE - replace motor

See ABB case # 59990 and carrier # 00757811. Replaced drive and lowered fla value in drive to match motor name plate of 12.6 from 15 amps. Changed minimum speed value in MBB to 67% from 33% to attempt to met air flow requirements of duct heaters and VAV boxes in tenant spaces. Unit should be fine but tenant comfort maybe impacted as it was before Unit change out as electric duct heaters not interlocked with unit blower. Heaters are dependent on air flow from RTU and have only air flow switches and limits to protect them. Installing contractor had to reset those limits to provide additional heat to those tenant spaces. Carrier may choice to view warranty claims with these preexisting short comings and misapplication issue in their determinations. Also no protection for static pressure of supply ducts or negative pressures in return ducts. Also tenant duct systems should be checked for proper returns and a total system review should be preformed to insure proper operation and optimal performance and comfort satisfaction. Start up forms and data plate pictures are attached within work order.

Found no refrigerant alarms in rtu.found alarm A410- vfd tripped out-overcurrent.reset alarm for rtu.checked vfd configs and rtu configs-ok.checked daily history in vfd-possible power issue when vfd tripped.fault history recorded dc bus voltage at 667v, 23Hz, 78.6 Amps, and 663 rpm.motor nameplate is 48.5 amps.restarted rtu and checked operations.amps are within specs with fan running at 100%- 39.8amps,42.6 amps, 37 amps.checked operations of rtu.rtu running with no alarms at this time.
